terms.title: Account ID
terms.summary: Identifier for an Iroha account composed of the domain it belongs to and the account controller (single key or multisig policy) that authorizes actions.
terms.definition: Identifier for an Iroha account composed of the domain it belongs to and the account controller (single key or multisig policy) that authorizes actions.
terms.tagline: Binds an account to its domain and authorization controller for deterministic identity resolution.

terms.title: Account Lifecycle
terms.summary: The sequence of register, update, rekey, and unregister operations that define how Iroha accounts are created and managed, enforced by on-chain permissions and admission policy.
terms.definition: The sequence of register, update, rekey, and unregister operations that define how Iroha accounts are created and managed, enforced by on-chain permissions and admission policy.
terms.tagline: Defines how accounts are created, modified, and retired under deterministic on-chain rules.

terms.title: Action
terms.summary: Trigger action payload that bundles the executable, repeats policy, authority, filter, and metadata defining what runs and when.
terms.definition: Trigger action payload that bundles the executable, repeats policy, authority, filter, and metadata defining what runs and when.
terms.tagline: Encapsulates the logic, authority, and firing policy behind a trigger.

terms.title: Activation Slot
terms.summary: Scheduled activation height or epoch for staged changes (for example, consensus mode, validator set, or manifest updates) so every node flips at the same block.
terms.definition: Scheduled activation height or epoch for staged changes (for example, consensus mode, validator set, or manifest updates) so every node flips at the same block.
terms.tagline: Lets governance stage changes for deterministic activation at a future height.

terms.title: Admission
terms.summary: Torii admission stage that validates transaction envelopes (Norito decode, signatures, chain ID, TTL, size limits) before enqueueing and gossip.
terms.definition: Torii admission stage that validates transaction envelopes (Norito decode, signatures, chain ID, TTL, size limits) before enqueueing and gossip.
terms.tagline: Rejects malformed or unauthorized transactions at the edge to protect the pipeline.

terms.title: Adoption
terms.summary: Adoption describes the rate at which people, partners, and institutions begin using SORA products, liquidity, and governance tooling in real-world contexts.
terms.definition: Adoption describes the rate at which people, partners, and institutions begin using SORA products, liquidity, and governance tooling in real-world contexts.
terms.tagline: Drives network effects and increases utility for all participants.

terms.title: Aggregation
terms.summary: Oracle aggregation step that combines observations into a consensus value using `AggregationRule` (median/MAD or percentile) after outlier and cap checks.
terms.definition: Oracle aggregation step that combines observations into a consensus value using `AggregationRule` (median/MAD or percentile) after outlier and cap checks.
terms.tagline: Turns multiple oracle reports into a single deterministic feed outcome.

terms.title: Agile Coretime
terms.summary: A flexible market where Polkadot sells coretime slices directly through brokered deals instead of fixed auctions.
terms.definition: Agile coretime lets projects purchase future execution capacity programmatically, smoothing demand and reducing the need for large upfront bids. It complements auctions and crowdloans by offering shorter-term or incremental commitments.

terms.title: Algorithmic Stability
terms.summary: Mechanisms that maintain stable asset value through programmatic supply adjustments—core to TBCD and SORA's monetary policy.
terms.definition: Algorithmic stability uses smart contracts and liquidity incentives to keep stablecoins near target value. SORA's Token Bonding Curve Dollar (TBCD) and Kensetsu architecture rely on algorithmic stability backed by governance oversight.

terms.title: AMM
terms.summary: Automated Market Maker - a protocol that uses mathematical formulas to price assets and provide liquidity automatically. Polkaswap uses AMM technology combined with liquidity ag…
terms.definition: Automated Market Maker - a protocol that uses mathematical formulas to price assets and provide liquidity automatically. Polkaswap uses AMM technology combined with liquidity aggregation to provide efficient trading with reduced impermanent loss.

terms.title: Analytics
terms.summary: Analytics covers the dashboards, telemetry, and research teams tracking SORA network health, liquidity depth, bridge flow, and ecosystem growth.
terms.definition: Analytics covers the dashboards, telemetry, and research teams tracking SORA network health, liquidity depth, bridge flow, and ecosystem growth.
terms.tagline: Enables data-driven decisions for network optimization.

terms.title: Apollo Protocol
terms.summary: A SORA ecosystem initiative focused on community-built tooling, analytics, and governance support for Polkaswap and SORA v3 upgrades.
terms.definition: Apollo Protocol coordinates community contributors who research tokenomics, publish knowledge base updates, and build automation for SORA releases. The group produces roadmap briefings, glossary enhancements, and documentation that keep builders aligned with Kensetsu, TBCD, and Polkaswap milestones.

terms.title: APOLLO Token
terms.summary: A community reward token used by the Apollo Protocol to incentivize research, documentation, and tooling for the SORA ecosystem.
terms.definition: The APOLLO token compensates contributors who publish technical research, produce analytics, and maintain documentation that supports SORA builders. Distribution is coordinated by the Apollo Protocol collective based on measurable ecosystem contributions.

terms.title: Assembly
terms.summary: Proposal assembly stage in the Sumeragi pipeline where the leader selects pending transactions, runs stateless/stateful checks, and builds a block proposal.
terms.definition: Proposal assembly stage in the Sumeragi pipeline where the leader selects pending transactions, runs stateless/stateful checks, and builds a block proposal.
terms.tagline: Builds a deterministic proposal from the pending set before voting begins.

terms.title: Asset Definition ID
terms.summary: Identifier of an asset definition composed of the asset name and domain, rendered as `name#domain`.
terms.definition: Identifier of an asset definition composed of the asset name and domain, rendered as `name#domain`.
terms.tagline: Defines an asset type within a domain for minting and transfers.

terms.title: Asset Tokenization
terms.summary: The process of issuing blockchain-based tokens that represent ownership of real-world or digital assets. SORA leverages tokenization to bring commodities, currencies, and projects on-chain.
terms.definition: Asset tokenization converts claims on physical or financial assets into programmable tokens. In SORA, tokenization is used to represent real-world assets, raise capital for new ventures, and create liquidity by listing these tokens on Polkaswap or other DeFi applications.

terms.title: Asynchronous Backing
terms.summary: A Polkadot upgrade that lets parachains submit work in parallel stages to raise throughput and lower latency.
terms.definition: Asynchronous backing separates block production, validation, and availability into overlapping phases. Validators can approve availability for one block while producing the next, increasing parachain capacity without compromising security.

terms.title: Attestations
terms.summary: Signed payloads used by Iroha subsystems (oracle binding, alias updates, jurisdiction policies, provider admission) to certify a claim under a defined schema and policy.
terms.definition: Signed payloads used by Iroha subsystems (oracle binding, alias updates, jurisdiction policies, provider admission) to certify a claim under a defined schema and policy.
terms.tagline: Provide verifiable claims that can be validated on-chain or by gateways.

terms.title: Attesters
terms.summary: Authorized signers or committees whose keys are configured to issue attestations (for example, DA sampling attesters, fraud monitoring engines, or alias attesters).
terms.definition: Authorized signers or committees whose keys are configured to issue attestations (for example, DA sampling attesters, fraud monitoring engines, or alias attesters).
terms.tagline: Only attestations from registered attesters are accepted by policy.

terms.title: Parachain Auctions
terms.summary: Candle-style events where Polkadot and Kusama projects bond DOT or KSM to lease parachain slots.
terms.definition: Parachain slot auctions determine which projects gain access to shared security for a fixed lease period. Bids accumulate until a randomized ending block is selected, encouraging honest bidding and staking participation through crowdloans.

terms.title: Automation
terms.summary: Deterministic on-chain workflows built with triggers: an executable plus filter and repeat policy that runs on schedules or events.
terms.definition: Deterministic on-chain workflows built with triggers: an executable plus filter and repeat policy that runs on schedules or events.
terms.tagline: Runs recurring or event-driven logic without off-chain bots.

terms.title: Bakong
terms.summary: Cambodia's national digital payment system built on blockchain technology by SORAMITSU. Bakong is one of the most successful CBDC implementations, with over 20 million users and…
terms.definition: Cambodia's national digital payment system built on blockchain technology by SORAMITSU. Bakong is one of the most successful CBDC implementations, with over 20 million users and $70 billion in transactions, demonstrating the potential of blockchain-based digital currencies.

terms.title: Bear Market
terms.summary: A market environment characterized by falling prices and defensive positioning.
terms.definition: Bear markets reflect sustained declines—commonly defined as drops of 20% or more—driven by risk aversion, deleveraging, or macro shocks. Strategies include conserving liquidity, diversifying collateral, and accelerating development to prepare for the next cycle.

terms.title: Bech32 Format
terms.summary: Bech32m-derived checksum envelope used in IH58/Iroha account addresses, providing a human-readable prefix and strong error detection.
terms.definition: Bech32m-derived checksum envelope used in IH58/Iroha account addresses, providing a human-readable prefix and strong error detection.
terms.tagline: Gives account identifiers a QR-friendly, checksum-protected format.

terms.title: BFT Consensus
terms.summary: Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) consensus is a consensus mechanism that allows a distributed system to reach agreement even when some nodes fail or act maliciously. SORA v3 uses…
terms.definition: Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) consensus is a consensus mechanism that allows a distributed system to reach agreement even when some nodes fail or act maliciously. SORA v3 uses BFT consensus derived from Hyperledger Iroha 3's architecture, providing high-throughput transaction processing with deterministic finality. This differs from SORA v2's Substrate-based consensus, offering improved security and performance for enterprise-grade applications including CBDCs.

terms.title: Bitcoin (BTC)
terms.summary: The first decentralized cryptocurrency, created by Satoshi Nakamoto in 2009 with a capped 21 million supply.
terms.definition: Bitcoin combines proof-of-work consensus, public-key cryptography, and halving-based issuance to secure peer-to-peer digital cash. Its monetary policy and liquidity cycles influence broader crypto markets, including assets listed on Polkaswap.

terms.title: BLAKE2b
terms.summary: Fast cryptographic hash function used throughout Iroha/Nexus for deterministic fingerprints and identifiers (for example, policy digests, proposal IDs, and content hashes).
terms.definition: Fast cryptographic hash function used throughout Iroha/Nexus for deterministic fingerprints and identifiers (for example, policy digests, proposal IDs, and content hashes).
terms.tagline: Fast, secure hashing for deterministic IDs and fingerprints.

terms.title: Blinded CIDs
terms.summary: Blinded content identifiers derived from a canonical CID and a published salt (domain-separated BLAKE3) so gateways can resolve content without exposing the original ID.
terms.definition: Blinded content identifiers derived from a canonical CID and a published salt (domain-separated BLAKE3) so gateways can resolve content without exposing the original ID.
terms.tagline: Allows gateway requests without revealing canonical manifest identifiers.

terms.title: Blockchain
terms.summary: A distributed ledger technology that maintains a continuously growing list of records secured using cryptography. SORA operates on blockchain technology, currently using Substra…
terms.definition: A distributed ledger technology that maintains a continuously growing list of records secured using cryptography. SORA operates on blockchain technology, currently using Substrate framework and transitioning to Hyperledger Iroha for enhanced enterprise capabilities.

terms.title: Blockchain Architecture
terms.summary: The design of blockchain components, including consensus, networking, data storage, and execution layers.
terms.definition: Blockchain architecture defines how nodes reach consensus, manage state, and upgrade over time. Reference models such as Substrate or Hyperledger Iroha separate the runtime, networking, and application layers to support modular upgrades and interoperability.

terms.title: Blockchain Culture
terms.summary: The shared narratives, rituals, and community norms that influence how blockchain networks grow and govern themselves.
terms.definition: Blockchain culture covers memes, language, social coordination, and incentive structures that shape contributor behavior. Understanding culture helps projects design governance, communication, and incentive programs that resonate with their communities.

links.label: Harvard Business Review – What Blockchain Can Do

terms.title: Blockchain Development
terms.summary: Engineering decentralized applications, smart contracts, and infrastructure that run on blockchain networks.
terms.definition: Blockchain development spans consensus clients, runtime modules, front-end interfaces, and integrations. Tooling such as Substrate, Hyperledger Iroha, and smart-contract frameworks enable teams to build features like Polkaswap, Kensetsu vaults, and cross-chain bridges.

terms.title: Blockchain Economics
terms.summary: The study of how token supply, incentives, and governance interact to sustain decentralized networks.
terms.definition: Blockchain economics analyzes monetary policy, reward distribution, and treasury design to keep participants aligned. Frameworks like the SORA token bonding curve illustrate how supply elasticity and governance controlled reserves stabilize ecosystem growth.

terms.title: Bokolo Cash
terms.summary: The Central Bank of Solomon Islands' digital currency pilot developed by SORAMITSU. Bokolo Cash demonstrates how SORA technology powers retail CBDCs with mobile-first payments.
terms.definition: Bokolo Cash is a CBDC project launched by the Central Bank of Solomon Islands and SORAMITSU. It uses SORA technology to deliver secure wallets, point-of-sale integrations, and compliance workflows that make digital currency available to citizens and merchants without traditional banking infrastructure.

terms.title: Bonding Curve
terms.summary: A smart contract that manages the supply of XOR in a rational way without human involvement. The TBC automatically adjusts XOR supply based on economic conditions to maintain price stability, expanding supply during growth and contracting during decline.
terms.definition: A smart contract that manages the supply of XOR in a rational way without human involvement. The TBC automatically adjusts XOR supply based on economic conditions to maintain price stability, expanding supply during growth and contracting during decline.

terms.title: Bonk (BONK)
terms.summary: A Solana-based meme token launched in 2022 that distributed a large airdrop to builders and NFT projects to revive Solana activity.
terms.definition: BONK runs on the Solana blockchain and uses token airdrops, liquidity incentives, and NFT partnerships to encourage ecosystem engagement. It highlights how meme assets can accelerate network usage outside of SORA.

terms.title: Borderless Finance
terms.summary: Borderless finance refers to financial services accessible globally without geographic restrictions. SORA enables borderless DeFi through permissionless access to Polkaswap, staking, and governance.
terms.definition: Borderless finance refers to financial services accessible globally without geographic restrictions. SORA enables borderless DeFi through permissionless access to Polkaswap, staking, and governance.

terms.title: Borrowing
terms.summary: Taking on debt against posted collateral using smart contracts that enforce repayment and liquidation rules.
terms.definition: Borrowing in DeFi involves locking approved collateral to mint or draw assets, paying stability fees until the position is closed. Kensetsu vaults on SORA apply governance-defined collateral ratios and liquidation procedures to keep the system solvent while providing access to KUSD or other approved assets.

terms.title: Bridges
terms.summary: Bridges are interoperability protocols that move assets and data between SORA and external chains so liquidity can circulate without centralized custodians.
terms.definition: Bridges are interoperability protocols that move assets and data between SORA and external chains so liquidity can circulate without centralized custodians.
terms.tagline: Connects SORA to the broader blockchain ecosystem.

terms.title: Budget
terms.summary: Configured resource caps (TEU budgets, gas limits, or subsystem quotas) that bound work per transaction or lane and keep scheduling deterministic.
terms.definition: Configured resource caps (TEU budgets, gas limits, or subsystem quotas) that bound work per transaction or lane and keep scheduling deterministic.
terms.tagline: Prevents any workflow from exceeding its allowed resource ceiling.

terms.title: Bull Market
terms.summary: A prolonged period of rising asset prices accompanied by expanding liquidity and optimism.
terms.definition: Bull markets occur when demand consistently outpaces supply, often supported by macro trends, innovation, or positive narratives. Participants may increase risk exposure, but prudent treasury management still prepares for eventual reversals.

terms.title: Buyback-and-burn
terms.summary: A tokenomic mechanism where tokens are purchased from the market and permanently destroyed. PSWAP uses a buyback-and-burn model where 0.3% of trading fees are used to buy PSWAP …
terms.definition: A tokenomic mechanism where tokens are purchased from the market and permanently destroyed. PSWAP uses a buyback-and-burn model where 0.3% of trading fees are used to buy PSWAP tokens from the market and burn them, reducing total supply and potentially increasing token value.

terms.title: Byzantine Fault Tolerance
terms.summary: Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) is a consensus property ensuring network operation even when some nodes act maliciously. SORA uses BFT-based SUMERAGI consensus for deterministic finality.
terms.definition: Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) is a consensus property ensuring network operation even when some nodes act maliciously. SORA uses BFT-based SUMERAGI consensus for deterministic finality.

terms.title: Canonical Primitives
terms.summary: Canonical encodings and algorithm choices baked into Iroha (hashing, signatures, Norito layouts) to keep deterministic outputs across nodes.
terms.definition: Canonical encodings and algorithm choices baked into Iroha (hashing, signatures, Norito layouts) to keep deterministic outputs across nodes.
terms.tagline: Keeps hashes, signatures, and encodings stable across the network.

terms.title: CBDC
terms.summary: Central Bank Digital Currency - a digital form of a country's fiat currency issued by the central bank. SORAMITSU has successfully deployed multiple CBDCs including Cambodia's B…
terms.definition: Central Bank Digital Currency - a digital form of a country's fiat currency issued by the central bank. SORAMITSU has successfully deployed multiple CBDCs including Cambodia's Bakong (8.5M users, $15.5M in payments), Lao CBDC pilot, and Fiji CBDC exploration. These blockchain-based systems enable financial inclusion, cross-border remittances, and interoperable digital payments.

terms.title: Ceres
terms.summary: A SORA-based DeFi suite providing launchpad services, stablecoins, and liquidity tools that complement Polkaswap.
terms.definition: Ceres offers decentralized applications such as Demeter Farming, SORA Card integrations, and liquidity vaults built on the SORA network. Its tooling accelerates adoption of Polkaswap pairs and supports Kensetsu stablecoin use cases.
terms.tagline: Provides essential DeFi infrastructure for projects building on SORA.

terms.title: Chain Discriminant
terms.summary: Per-network 16-bit value reused as the IH58 network prefix so account addresses self-identify their Sora Nexus chain and avoid cross-network collisions.
terms.definition: Per-network 16-bit value reused as the IH58 network prefix so account addresses self-identify their Sora Nexus chain and avoid cross-network collisions.
terms.tagline: The numeric network prefix embedded in IH58 addresses.

terms.title: Chain ID
terms.summary: Unique chain identifier configured per network and checked in transaction/admission flows to bind artifacts to the intended ledger and prevent cross-chain replay.
terms.definition: Unique chain identifier configured per network and checked in transaction/admission flows to bind artifacts to the intended ledger and prevent cross-chain replay.
terms.tagline: Binds transactions and consensus artifacts to a specific network.

terms.title: Chainlink
terms.summary: A decentralized oracle network that provides tamper-resistant data feeds and automation services to smart contracts. SORA integrates Chainlink oracles to bridge real-world data for DeFi and RWA products.
terms.definition: Chainlink delivers cryptographic proofs and reliable data to smart contracts. On SORA, Chainlink price feeds and automation support Polkaswap trading pairs, collateral monitoring for tokenized assets, and cross-chain messaging for enterprise integrations.

terms.title: Circuit Breakers
terms.summary: Safety guardrails that halt or restrict execution when liquidity, governance, or oracle policies trip, surfaced as circuit-breaker errors.
terms.definition: Safety guardrails that halt or restrict execution when liquidity, governance, or oracle policies trip, surfaced as circuit-breaker errors.
terms.tagline: Stops execution when safety guards are active.

terms.title: Circuit-Breaker State
terms.summary: State and telemetry describing which circuit breaker kind is active for a dataspace, surfaced in error context and monitoring APIs.
terms.definition: State and telemetry describing which circuit breaker kind is active for a dataspace, surfaced in error context and monitoring APIs.
terms.tagline: Explains why execution was halted and when it can resume.

terms.title: Citizenship
terms.summary: A status in the SORA Parliament governance system where individuals become citizens by posting XOR bonds. Citizens are randomly selected through sortition to participate in vari…
terms.definition: A status in the SORA Parliament governance system where individuals become citizens by posting XOR bonds. Citizens are randomly selected through sortition to participate in various governance bodies and make decisions about XOR allocation to productive projects.

terms.title: Collateral
terms.summary: Assets pledged to secure loans or stablecoin issuance. Collateral design determines the safety of SORA's future lending products.
terms.definition: Collateral provides assurance that loans can be repaid or liquidated. SORA plans to accept XOR, stablecoins, and real-world assets as collateral for Kensetsu vaults, combining decentralized governance with transparent risk metrics.

links.label: SORA Token Bonding Curve Dollar Explained

terms.title: Collateralized Locks
terms.summary: Escrowed funds backing offline-offline vouchers, providing settlement guarantees until reconciliation clears or revokes the transfer.
terms.definition: Escrowed funds backing offline-offline vouchers, providing settlement guarantees until reconciliation clears or revokes the transfer.
terms.tagline: Enables secure offline payments that settle atomically when parties reconnect.

terms.title: Commitments
terms.summary: Canonical DA commitment records and bundles that bind manifest hashes, chunk roots, and proof schemes to a block and are hashed into the block header.
terms.definition: Canonical DA commitment records and bundles that bind manifest hashes, chunk roots, and proof schemes to a block and are hashed into the block header.
terms.tagline: Bind data-availability proofs and metadata to blocks for auditing.

terms.title: Commit Window
terms.summary: Configured slot budget for proofs and DA bundles to arrive before a transaction aborts, encoded in commit timing parameters.
terms.definition: Configured slot budget for proofs and DA bundles to arrive before a transaction aborts, encoded in commit timing parameters.
terms.tagline: Defines how long the system waits for required proofs or DA evidence.

terms.title: Community
terms.summary: The SORA community comprises developers, validators, liquidity providers, governance participants, and users who collectively shape the network direction through proposals, discussions, and on-chain voting.
terms.definition: The SORA community comprises developers, validators, liquidity providers, governance participants, and users who collectively shape the network direction through proposals, discussions, and on-chain voting.

terms.title: Compute Lane
terms.summary: A lane that accepts deterministic HTTP-style compute calls, routes them to Kotodama entrypoints via a manifest, and records metering/receipts for billing and governance review.
terms.definition: A lane that accepts deterministic HTTP-style compute calls, routes them to Kotodama entrypoints via a manifest, and records metering/receipts for billing and governance review.
terms.tagline: Deterministic compute routes with sandbox rules and metering.

terms.title: Compute Manifest
terms.summary: A manifest binding service/method routes to Kotodama entrypoints with a namespace, ABI version, sandbox guardrails, codec allowlists, and per-route limits (TTL, gas, size, auth, determinism).
terms.definition: A manifest binding service/method routes to Kotodama entrypoints with a namespace, ABI version, sandbox guardrails, codec allowlists, and per-route limits (TTL, gas, size, auth, determinism).
terms.tagline: Defines which compute routes are allowed and how they execute.

terms.title: Concurrency
terms.summary: The ability of a system to handle multiple tasks or processes overlapping in time.
terms.definition: Concurrency techniques—such as threads, async executors, and message passing—allow software to utilize multi-core hardware and keep I/O operations non-blocking. SORA infrastructure written in Rust relies on disciplined concurrency to maintain reliability.

terms.title: Condition
terms.summary: The event filter attached to a trigger action that decides when the executable fires (data events, pipeline events, or time events).
terms.definition: The event filter attached to a trigger action that decides when the executable fires (data events, pipeline events, or time events).
terms.tagline: Filters events before a trigger action executes.

terms.title: Consensus
terms.summary: The mechanism by which blockchain networks agree on the validity of transactions and maintain a consistent state. SORA v2 uses Substrate-based consensus mechanisms (NPoS - Nomin…
terms.definition: The mechanism by which blockchain networks agree on the validity of transactions and maintain a consistent state. SORA v2 uses Substrate-based consensus mechanisms (NPoS - Nominated Proof of Stake). SORA v3 will use Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) consensus derived from Hyperledger Iroha 3's architecture, providing high-throughput transaction processing with deterministic finality, making it suitable for enterprise applications and CBDCs.

terms.title: Coretime
terms.summary: The compute resource that Polkadot sells to projects so they can execute workloads on relay-chain validators.
terms.definition: Coretime packages validator execution capacity into timeslices that projects buy via auctions or agile markets. Managing coretime commitments helps parachains plan throughput needs, budget DOT expenditures, and coordinate upgrades.

terms.title: Council
terms.summary: A governance body in SORA's current Polkadot v1 governance system that consists of elected members who can propose referenda and veto dangerous proposals. The council plays a key role in the governance process before transitioning to the SORA Parliament.
terms.definition: A governance body in SORA's current Polkadot v1 governance system that consists of elected members who can propose referenda and veto dangerous proposals. The council plays a key role in the governance process before transitioning to the SORA Parliament.
terms.tagline: Ensures community oversight of network development.

terms.title: Council Motion
terms.summary: A proposal submitted by the SORA Council in the current governance system. When a council motion is approved, it triggers a Democracy Referendum where token holders can vote on …
terms.definition: A proposal submitted by the SORA Council in the current governance system. When a council motion is approved, it triggers a Democracy Referendum where token holders can vote on the proposal, enabling community participation in governance decisions.

terms.title: Cross-Border Corridors
terms.summary: A deployment pattern that connects multiple jurisdictions or payment systems using Nexus lanes and ISO 20022 connectors; corridor rules and liquidity live in governance and applications, not core protocol types.
terms.definition: A deployment pattern that connects multiple jurisdictions or payment systems using Nexus lanes and ISO 20022 connectors; corridor rules and liquidity live in governance and applications, not core protocol types.
terms.tagline: A business corridor built on lanes plus ISO 20022 integration.

terms.title: Cross-border Payments
terms.summary: Financial transactions between parties in different countries. CBDC implementations like Bakong enable faster, cheaper, and more efficient cross-border remittances by using bloc…
terms.definition: Financial transactions between parties in different countries. CBDC implementations like Bakong enable faster, cheaper, and more efficient cross-border remittances by using blockchain technology to reduce intermediaries and settlement times.

terms.title: Cross-Chain
terms.summary: The ability to transfer assets and data between different blockchain networks. SORA enables cross-chain functionality through bridges and interoperability protocols, allowing us…
terms.definition: The ability to transfer assets and data between different blockchain networks. SORA enables cross-chain functionality through bridges and interoperability protocols, allowing users to trade assets from different blockchains on Polkaswap.

terms.title: Crowdloans
terms.summary: Campaigns that let token holders bond assets to support a project's parachain auction bid.
terms.definition: Crowdloans escrow contributor DOT or KSM on the relay chain, returning the stake after the lease while projects distribute rewards separately. They democratize access to parachain slots and align community incentives with network growth.

terms.title: Cryptography
terms.summary: Cryptography in blockchain provides security through digital signatures, hash functions, and encryption. SORA uses Ed25519, BLAKE2b, and other primitives to secure accounts and transactions.
terms.definition: Cryptography in blockchain provides security through digital signatures, hash functions, and encryption. SORA uses Ed25519, BLAKE2b, and other primitives to secure accounts and transactions.

terms.title: Crypto Market Cycles
terms.summary: Recurring bull and bear phases observed in cryptocurrency markets. Understanding cycles informs staking, liquidity, and treasury decisions in the SORA ecosystem.
terms.definition: Crypto market cycles describe periods of expansion and contraction driven by macro events, liquidity, and investor sentiment. SORA tracks these cycles to plan token issuance, liquidity incentives, and treasury diversification so that builders can deploy capital efficiently.

terms.title: Curve25519
terms.summary: The elliptic curve underlying Ed25519 signatures (and X25519 key agreement), used by Iroha's default signature scheme.
terms.definition: The elliptic curve underlying Ed25519 signatures (and X25519 key agreement), used by Iroha's default signature scheme.
terms.tagline: The curve behind Ed25519.

terms.title: DA Certificates
terms.summary: Attester-signed certificates that sampled and verified erasure-coded shards for a data space, used by the nexus committee to accept DA without pulling shards.
terms.definition: Attester-signed certificates that sampled and verified erasure-coded shards for a data space, used by the nexus committee to accept DA without pulling shards.
terms.tagline: Proof that DA sampling succeeded in-slot.

terms.title: DA Sampling
terms.summary: VRF-sampled attesters check a subset of erasure-coded shards each slot and sign availability; sample size and thresholds are deterministic config.
terms.definition: VRF-sampled attesters check a subset of erasure-coded shards each slot and sign availability; sample size and thresholds are deterministic config.
terms.tagline: Randomized shard checks to detect withholding.

terms.title: DA Sampling Budget
terms.summary: Deterministic caps on in-slot DA signatures per lane and per dataspace, plus per-attester shard checks, so sampling work stays bounded.
terms.definition: Deterministic caps on in-slot DA signatures per lane and per dataspace, plus per-attester shard checks, so sampling work stays bounded.
terms.tagline: Limits DA sampling work per slot.

terms.title: DA Sampling Confidence
terms.summary: The sampling confidence target derived from sample sizes (S) and threshold (T) for DA certificates, controlling how many attester signatures are required.
terms.definition: The sampling confidence target derived from sample sizes (S) and threshold (T) for DA certificates, controlling how many attester signatures are required.
terms.tagline: Sets how much sampling is enough to accept availability.

terms.title: Data Availability
terms.summary: Erasure-coded Kura/WSV blobs with Merkle commitments in headers; DA attesters sample shards and issue certificates so blocks can commit without downloading full data.
terms.definition: Erasure-coded Kura/WSV blobs with Merkle commitments in headers; DA attesters sample shards and issue certificates so blocks can commit without downloading full data.
terms.tagline: Commitments plus sampling make blobs retrievable.

terms.title: Data Availability Layer
terms.summary: The DA subsystem: erasure-coded storage, shard sampling, attester certificates, and retrieval policies for public vs private data spaces.
terms.definition: The DA subsystem: erasure-coded storage, shard sampling, attester certificates, and retrieval policies for public vs private data spaces.
terms.tagline: Provides retrievability for blobs while preserving privacy boundaries.

terms.title: Data Envelope
terms.summary: An ISO 20022 wrapper element (DataEnvelope/DataPDU/Body) that the IVM canonicalizer strips when deriving message paths and hashes.
terms.definition: An ISO 20022 wrapper element (DataEnvelope/DataPDU/Body) that the IVM canonicalizer strips when deriving message paths and hashes.
terms.tagline: Outer ISO 20022 wrapper ignored for canonical paths.

terms.title: Data Space Directory

terms.definition: On-chain registry of Space Directory manifests (AssetPermissionManifest) keyed by UAID and DataSpaceId, with publish/revoke/expire lifecycle.

Hyperledger Iroha 2 (written in Rust) adds WASM smart contracts and improved performance, making it suitable for enterprise systems, CBDCs, and national-level financial infrastructure.
terms.tagline: Powers enterprise blockchain with production-proven reliability.

terms.title: Iroha3
terms.summary: Hyperledger Iroha 3 is the next-generation blockchain framework being developed for SORA v3 (Nexus). Hyperledger Iroha 3 introduces a re-engineered architecture with greater modularity, new consensus mechanisms, and enhanced security primitives. It features layered runtime for domain-specific modules, upgraded command model, query isolation for deterministic operations, and simplified validator orchestration. Hyperledger Iroha 3 will support Iroha Special Instructions (ISIs) for deterministic smart-contract logic and provide the foundation for SORA v3's high-performance, cross-chain infrastructure.

terms.title: KUSD
terms.summary: Kensetsu USD (KUSD) is an over-collateralized, algorithmically governed stablecoin built on the SORA network, pegged to the US Dollar. Built on the Kensetsu Platform (SORA's ver…
terms.definition: Kensetsu USD (KUSD) is an over-collateralized, algorithmically governed stablecoin built on the SORA network, pegged to the US Dollar. Built on the Kensetsu Platform (SORA's version of MakerDAO), KUSD facilitates secure borrowing operations while maintaining its value through robust stability mechanisms. In SORA v3 tokenomics, KUSD is used to pay builders instead of XOR. To maintain the KUSD peg, 19.5% of all SORA network transaction fees are allocated for buyback and burning of KUSD. Users can create vaults, deposit collateral (XOR, VAL, PSWAP, TBCD, ETH, or DAI), and borrow KUSD against their collateral.
terms.tagline: Provides stable value for trading, payments, and DeFi without relying on centralized custodians.

terms.title: Lambda Floor

terms.definition: The approximately one-second confirmation target each lane's SUMERAGI pipeline in SORA Nexus reaches before merge ordering combines outputs with other parallel lanes.
terms.tagline: Enables parallel transaction processing while maintaining global ordering guarantees.

terms.title: Lane Fusion

Parachains can specialize in specific use cases (DeFi, privacy, smart contracts) while maintaining interoperability through Cross-Consensus Messaging (XCM). They process transactions in parallel and are validated by the relay chain's validator set.

terms.title: Parachains

terms.definition: Parachains are independent blockchains that connect to the Polkadot or Kusama relay chain for shared security and cross-chain messaging. SORA operates as a parachain, benefiting from Polkadot consensus while maintaining its own specialized runtime.

terms.definition: The architectural pattern in SORA Nexus of running multiple lanes simultaneously to boost throughput horizontally without spawning separate chains or fragmenting liquidity.

terms.definition: The ability to process multiple transactions simultaneously across different blockchain networks. Polkadot parachains enable parallel processing by allowing multiple parachains to process transactions in parallel, significantly increasing overall network throughput compared to sequential processing.

terms.title: Parameter Sets
terms.summary: Versioned on-chain collections in SORA Nexus of cryptography choices, admission caps, and scheduler knobs that governance can update without requiring hard forks.
terms.definition: Versioned on-chain collections in SORA Nexus of cryptography choices, admission caps, and scheduler knobs that governance can update without requiring hard forks.
terms.tagline: Lets the network tune performance and security without redeploying code.

terms.title: Parathreads
terms.summary: On-demand parachain slots that pay for execution per block instead of committing to a full lease.
terms.definition: Parathreads let projects share coretime in a pay-as-you-go model, ideal for lower throughput applications or pilots. They can later transition into full parachains once usage justifies a dedicated lease.

terms.title: Parliament
terms.summary: The future democratic governance system of SORA using multi-body sortition with clear separation of powers. The SORA Parliament will replace the current Governance V1 system, implementing sortition-based democracy where citizens are randomly selected (not token voting) and must post XOR bonds for citizenship. Features multiple bodies: Rules Committee, Agenda Council, Interest Panels, Review Panel, and Policy Jury. Main task is allocating newly minted XOR to productive projects. In SORA v3, the Parliament will integrate with a hybrid DAO framework using Iroha Special Instructions (ISIs) for modular governance logic.

terms.tagline: Enables fair representation through democratic lottery selection.

terms.definition: PEPE is an ERC-20 token themed after the Pepe the Frog meme. It has no formal roadmap or presale and relies on community-led liquidity pools, illustrating the speculative dynamics that influence wider crypto markets.

terms.definition: Performance analysis measures throughput, latency, and resource utilization to spot bottlenecks. Optimizing performance is crucial for blockchain clients, smart contracts, and front-end applications that must stay responsive under load.

terms.definition: A heterogeneous multi-chain network that enables different blockchains to transfer messages and value in a trust-free fashion. Polkadot provides shared security, cross-chain interoperability, and parallel processing through its relay chain and parachain architecture.

terms.title: Polkadot Governance
terms.summary: The governance system used by Polkadot and its parachains. SORA v2 uses Polkadot v1 Governance (also called Governance V1), which features council-based proposals, referendum vo…
terms.definition: The governance system used by Polkadot and its parachains. SORA v2 uses Polkadot v1 Governance (also called Governance V1), which features council-based proposals, referendum voting, and technical committee oversight. This differs from Polkadot OpenGov, which SORA does not currently use. Governance V1 provides a robust framework for network decision-making with predictable proposal cycles.

terms.title: Polkaswap
terms.summary: A next-generation, cross-chain liquidity aggregator DEX protocol built on SORA network. Polkaswap aggregates liquidity from multiple sources (AMM DEXs, order books, algorithms) …
terms.definition: A next-generation, cross-chain liquidity aggregator DEX protocol built on SORA network. Polkaswap aggregates liquidity from multiple sources (AMM DEXs, order books, algorithms) and provides smart liquidity routing to find the best prices. It enables seamless trading of ETH/ERC-20 tokens, DOT/KSM, BTC, and future assets with high speed, low fees, and reduced impermanent loss through its unique liquidity infrastructure.
terms.tagline: Enables permissionless trading with best-price routing across multiple liquidity sources.

terms.title: Poseidon2

terms.definition: The algebraic hash function optimized for zero-knowledge circuits in SORA Nexus, used extensively in FASTPQ commitments, Sparse Merkle Trees, and state proofs.

terms.title: PoW Ticket

terms.definition: Hashcash-style proof-of-work token attached to SoraNet circuit establishment, containing difficulty, expiry, and nonces; relays validate it to throttle abuse and gate certain capabilities.
terms.tagline: Proof-of-work admission token for circuits.

terms.definition: Signed value chits bound to a snapshot and revocation window, enabling offline-offline payments with later reconciliation.

terms.title: Price Optimization

terms.definition: Price optimization refers to mechanisms that improve trade execution and reduce slippage. Polkaswap aggregates multiple liquidity sources and uses smart order routing for optimal swap prices.

terms.title: Price Stability

terms.definition: The maintenance of relatively stable token prices over time through economic mechanisms. SORA's Token Bonding Curve maintains XOR price stability by automatically adjusting supply based on market conditions - expanding supply during price increases and contracting during price decreases.

terms.title: Privacy Transactions

terms.definition: Shielded transaction flows in SORA Nexus that keep amounts and participants confidential via Halo2 circuits, commitments, and nullifiers while maintaining auditability.
terms.tagline: Ensures privacy by routing traffic through multiple relay nodes.

terms.definition: Permissioned partitions in SORA Nexus where data and proofs remain within the operator's trust boundary, using ML-DSA-87 attestations for data availability while maintaining regulatory compliance.
terms.tagline: Allows enterprises and institutions to participate in SORA Nexus while keeping sensitive data confidential and compliant with local regulations.

terms.title: Programming
terms.summary: The act of designing and writing instructions that computers execute.
terms.definition: Programming involves translating requirements into source code, testing, and maintaining software. Blockchain initiatives rely on languages such as Rust, TypeScript, and Python to build clients, tooling, and user interfaces.

terms.title: Proof of Stake (PoS)
terms.summary: A consensus mechanism where validators stake tokens to secure the network. SORA v2 uses NPoS on Substrate while SORA v3 moves toward BFT consensus.
terms.definition: Proof of Stake selects validators based on staked assets rather than energy expenditure. The model incentivizes honest behavior by slashing or rewarding stake. SORA references PoS to explain historical network phases and to contrast with Hyperledger Iroha's BFT consensus.

terms.title: Proof of Work (PoW)
terms.summary: A consensus method where miners expend computational energy to propose blocks and earn rewards.
terms.definition: Proof of Work secures networks such as Bitcoin by requiring miners to solve cryptographic puzzles. The difficulty adjusts to maintain steady block production, making attacks costly because adversaries must control the majority of hashing power.

terms.title: Proof Systems
terms.summary: The combination of FASTPQ STARKs, Halo2 circuits, and supporting protocols that provide verifiable execution and privacy.
terms.definition: The combination of FASTPQ STARKs, Halo2 circuits, and supporting protocols that provide verifiable execution and privacy.

terms.definition: The per-slot time allocation (100 - 200 ms typical) reserved for lane committees to check proofs without falling behind.

terms.definition: A proposal is a formal request submitted to SORA governance for funding, parameter changes, or new initiatives that citizens can evaluate.
terms.tagline: Gives every community member a voice in network decisions.

terms.title: Provers

terms.definition: Actors in SORA Nexus (often GPU-accelerated) that generate FASTPQ or DA proofs and deliver them within configured latency budgets to maintain network throughput.

terms.definition: A deflationary token used to reward liquidity providers on Polkaswap. PSWAP has a 10 billion max supply that decreases over time, with 0.3% trading fees used for buyback-and-burn, and rewards starting at 90% of burned tokens reminted for LPs, decreasing to 35% after 5 years.
terms.tagline: Rewards users who provide liquidity, creating sustainable DeFi incentives.

terms.title: Public Data Spaces
terms.summary: Open participation domains in SORA Nexus where data availability sampling is performed publicly and Ed25519 signatures attest to availability, enabling transparent verification by any network participant.
terms.definition: Open participation domains in SORA Nexus where data availability sampling is performed publicly and Ed25519 signatures attest to availability, enabling transparent verification by any network participant.

terms.title: QR Payments
terms.summary: Payments completed by scanning a Quick Response (QR) code. QR flows are widely used in SORA Card pilots and CBDC deployments to provide low-cost merchant acceptance.
terms.definition: QR payments encode payment instructions in a scannable code that can be read by mobile devices. They remove the need for specialized hardware, letting SORA Card users and CBDC pilots like Bokolo Cash settle transactions instantly while retaining on-chain auditability.

terms.title: Quorum Certificate
terms.summary: An aggregated signature set (≥2f+1 validators) certifying a proposal, forming the foundation of SUMERAGI's safety guarantees.
terms.definition: An aggregated signature set (≥2f+1 validators) certifying a proposal, forming the foundation of SUMERAGI's safety guarantees.
terms.tagline: Proves supermajority agreement on a block, enabling light clients to verify finality with minimal data.

terms.title: Real-World Assets
terms.summary: Physical or traditional financial assets represented on-chain, such as commodities, invoices, or government bonds. Tokenizing RWAs expands Polkaswap liquidity and supports SORA's economic initiatives.
terms.definition: Real-world assets (RWAs) are tangible or regulated assets that become programmable once they are tokenized. SORA uses RWAs to collateralize stable instruments, fund infrastructure projects, and provide transparent reporting to stakeholders.

terms.title: Redenomination
terms.summary: The process of adjusting token denominations without changing total value. SORA redenominated XOR in 2020 to improve usability and align token supply with long-term monetary policy.
terms.definition: Redenomination changes the nominal unit of account by splitting or combining circulating supply while preserving proportional ownership. SORA implemented a 1:100 XOR redenomination coordinated through on-chain governance to simplify pricing, rebalance treasury reserves, and prepare for the token bonding curve monetary system.

terms.title: Reed-solomon
terms.summary: The erasure-coding scheme used in SORA Nexus for row and column parity in SoraFS, ensuring any k-of-n shards can reconstruct the original data envelope.
terms.definition: The erasure-coding scheme used in SORA Nexus for row and column parity in SoraFS, ensuring any k-of-n shards can reconstruct the original data envelope.
terms.tagline: Provides mathematical guarantees that data survives validator failures or network partitions.

terms.definition: A Democracy Referendum in SORA's current governance system (Polkadot v1 Governance, also called Governance V1). After a Council Motion is approved by the SORA Council, it becomes a Democracy Referendum where the entire community can vote on specific proposals, parameter changes, or network upgrades. This differs from Polkadot OpenGov, which SORA v2 does not use.

terms.title: Relay Chain
terms.summary: The central chain of the Polkadot network that provides security, consensus, and cross-chain interoperability for all connected parachains. The relay chain coordinates the entir…
terms.definition: The central chain of the Polkadot network that provides security, consensus, and cross-chain interoperability for all connected parachains. The relay chain coordinates the entire network and enables shared security across all parachains.

terms.title: REST Gateways

terms.definition: HTTP interfaces that expose Norito-first APIs for developers who prefer REST semantics over gRPC. These gateways provide deterministic transaction builders, ISO 20022 helpers, and offline flow support, with receipts and proofs aligned to protocol primitives for web and mobile SDK integration.
terms.tagline: Enables familiar HTTP access to SORA Nexus for web and mobile developers.

terms.title: Revocation Windows

terms.definition: Bounded time intervals in SORA Nexus during which off-chain vouchers can be canceled if reconciliation uncovers fraud, protecting users from delayed attack vectors.

terms.definition: Incentives distributed to network participants for contributing to network operations. In SORA, rewards include VAL tokens for validators and stakers, PSWAP tokens for liquidity providers, and XOR allocations for productive projects through governance.

terms.definition: The roadmap outlines upcoming SORA releases, TON integrations, and ecosystem milestones so contributors share the same delivery plan.

terms.summary: Scaling solutions that execute transactions off-chain and submit proofs or bundles on-chain for security.
terms.definition: Rollups batch transactions, compress state transitions, and post validity or fraud proofs to a base layer. They lower fees while retaining trust minimization, complementing approaches like Hyperledger Iroha's deterministic consensus.

terms.definition: Rust is a systems programming language known for memory safety and performance. SORA and Hyperledger Iroha 2 are built with Rust, enabling secure, high-throughput blockchain execution with compile-time guarantees against common vulnerabilities.

terms.title: Rust
terms.summary: A systems programming language focused on memory safety, concurrency, and performance.
terms.definition: Rust eliminates most classes of memory errors through ownership and borrowing rules, making it popular for blockchain clients and cryptography. Hyperledger Iroha 2 and 3, key components of SORA v3, are implemented in Rust to benefit from its safety guarantees.

terms.title: Scalability

terms.title: Scarcity

terms.definition: Scarcity in tokenomics refers to limited supply that can drive value. SORA manages scarcity through the Token Bonding Curve, which algorithmically controls XOR minting based on economic conditions.

terms.title: Scarcity Economics

terms.definition: Scarcity economics studies how limited supply affects pricing and behavior. XOR uses algorithmic elasticity to balance scarcity with utility, ensuring the network can scale while preserving long-term value for participants.

terms.definition: Self-executing contracts with the terms of the agreement directly written into code. In SORA, smart contracts like the Token Bonding Curve automatically manage token supply and economic parameters without human intervention.

terms.title: Smart Contracts
terms.summary: Smart contracts are self-executing programs stored on blockchain that automatically enforce agreement terms. SORA supports smart contracts through Ink! (Rust-based) and future WASM execution environments.
terms.definition: Smart contracts are self-executing programs stored on blockchain that automatically enforce agreement terms. SORA supports smart contracts through Ink! (Rust-based) and future WASM execution environments.

terms.title: Smart Routing
terms.summary: An algorithm that automatically finds the optimal path for trading to minimize slippage and maximize returns. Polkaswap's smart routing analyzes multiple liquidity sources and a…
terms.definition: An algorithm that automatically finds the optimal path for trading to minimize slippage and maximize returns. Polkaswap's smart routing analyzes multiple liquidity sources and automatically routes trades through the best available pools to provide optimal pricing.

terms.title: SNX HRP
terms.summary: Human-readable prefix (`snx`) used in the Bech32m-style checksum for Sora-only compressed account addresses, improving error detection and keeping the checksum domain-separated from other formats.
terms.definition: Human-readable prefix (`snx`) used in the Bech32m-style checksum for Sora-only compressed account addresses, improving error detection and keeping the checksum domain-separated from other formats.
